	// JavaScript, so the authored `./x.ts` specifier has to become `./x.js` in
	// the output, which is exactly what the third option does.
	if options.AllowImportingTsExtensions.IsTrue() && !options.NoEmit.IsTrue() && !options.EmitDeclarationOnly.IsTrue() {
		options.RewriteRelativeImportExtensions = core.TSTrue
	}
	return options, rejections, nil
}

func defaultLanguageLibraries(options *core.CompilerOptions) ([]string, error) {
	// The native loader accepts *.full.d.ts only through its implicit-default
	// branch, not GetLibFileName's explicit lib registry. Read the pinned
	// aggregator's own native-parsed references instead of copying a target/lib
	// table that can drift from upstream (including its DOM/worker defaults).
	name := tspath.CombinePaths(bundled.LibPath(), tsoptions.GetDefaultLibFileName(options))
	text, ok := bundled.WrapFS(vfstest.FromMap(map[string]string{}, true)).ReadFile(name)
	if !ok {
		return nil, errors.New("bundled default language library is unavailable")
	}
	file := parser.ParseSourceFile(ast.SourceFileParseOptions{FileName: name, Path: tspath.Path(name)}, text, core.ScriptKindTS)
	if len(file.Diagnostics()) != 0 || len(file.Statements.Nodes) != 0 || len(file.ReferencedFiles) != 0 || len(file.LibReferenceDirectives) == 0 {
		return nil, errors.New("bundled default language library is not a reference aggregator")
	}
	libraries := make([]string, 0, len(file.LibReferenceDirectives)+1)
	for _, reference := range file.LibReferenceDirectives {
		library, known := tsoptions.GetLibFileName(reference.FileName)
		if !known {
			return nil, errors.New("bundled default language library has an unknown reference")
		}
		libraries = append(libraries, library)
	}
	return append(libraries, "lib.esnext.disposable.d.ts"), nil
}

func tristate(value any) (core.Tristate, error) {
	parsed, ok := value.(bool)
	if !ok {
		return core.TSUnknown, fmt.Errorf("must be a boolean")
	}
	if parsed {
		return core.TSTrue, nil
	}
	return core.TSFalse, nil
}

func optionError(name string, err error) error {
	return fmt.Errorf("compiler option %q %w", name, err)
}

func virtualFileName(logical string) (string, error) {
	logical = strings.ReplaceAll(logical, "\\", "/")
	if strings.HasPrefix(logical, "/") || strings.Contains(logical, ":") {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("compiler input path %q must be relative", logical)
	}
	clean := path.Clean(logical)
	if clean == "." || clean == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(clean, "../") {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("compiler input path %q escapes the virtual project", logical)
	}
	return "/src/" + clean, nil
}

func emittedFileName(fileName string) string {
	fileName = strings.ReplaceAll(fileName, "\\", "/")
	return strings.TrimPrefix(fileName, "/out/")
}

func categoryName(category diagnostics.Category) string {
	switch category {
	case diagnostics.CategoryWarning:
		return "warning"
	case diagnostics.CategoryError:
		return "error"
	case diagnostics.CategorySuggestion:
		return "suggestion"
	case diagnostics.CategoryMessage:
		return "message"
	default:
		return "error"
	}
}

// lineIndex converts between byte offsets and (line, UTF-16 column) positions
// of one immutable text. Line boundaries follow TypeScript: CRLF is one break;
// bare CR, LF, U+2028 and U+2029 are also breaks, not source-map columns.
type lineIndex struct {
	text             string
	starts           []int
	utf16Checkpoints []utf16Checkpoint
	ascii            bool
}

type utf16Checkpoint struct{ byteOffset, codeUnits int }

func newLineIndex(text string) *lineIndex {
	starts := []int{0}
	checkpoints := []utf16Checkpoint{{}}
	units := 0
	ascii := true
	for offset, character := range text {
		if character >= 128 {
			ascii = false
		}
		// Checkpoints are rune boundaries. Even a caller-provided offset inside
		// a UTF-8 sequence retains utf16Extent's previous replacement semantics.
		if offset-checkpoints[len(checkpoints)-1].byteOffset >= 1024 {
			checkpoints = append(checkpoints, utf16Checkpoint{byteOffset: offset, codeUnits: units})
		}
		switch character {
		case '\n':
			starts = append(starts, offset+1)
		case '\r':
			if offset+1 == len(text) || text[offset+1] != '\n' {
				starts = append(starts, offset+1)
			}
		case '\u2028', '\u2029':
			starts = append(starts, offset+3)
		}
		units += utf16RuneLen(character)
	}
	return &lineIndex{text: text, starts: starts, utf16Checkpoints: checkpoints, ascii: ascii}
}

func (index *lineIndex) lineCount() int { return len(index.starts) }

func (index *lineIndex) lineText(line int) string {
	if line < 0 || line >= len(index.starts) {
		return ""
	}
	start := index.starts[line]
	end := len(index.text)
	if line+1 < len(index.starts) {
		end = index.starts[line+1]
		if index.text[end-1] == '\n' {
			end--
			if end > start && index.text[end-1] == '\r' {
				end--
			}
		} else if index.text[end-1] == '\r' {
			end--
		} else {
			end -= 3 // UTF-8 U+2028 / U+2029
		}
	}
	return index.text[start:end]
}

func (index *lineIndex) utf16Length(line int) int {
	if index.ascii {
		return len(index.lineText(line))
	}
	return utf16Extent(index.lineText(line))
}

func (index *lineIndex) position(byteOffset int) (line int, utf16Column int) {
	if byteOffset < 0 {
		byteOffset = 0
	}
	if byteOffset > len(index.text) {
		byteOffset = len(index.text)
	}
	low, high := 0, len(index.starts)-1
	for low < high {
		middle := (low + high + 1) / 2
		if index.starts[middle] <= byteOffset {
			low = middle
		} else {
			high = middle - 1
		}
	}
	if index.ascii {
		return low, byteOffset - index.starts[low]
	}
	return low, utf16Extent(index.text[index.starts[low]:byteOffset])
}

func (index *lineIndex) byteOffset(line int, utf16Column int) int {
	if line < 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if line >= len(index.starts) {
		return len(index.text)
	}
	lineText := index.lineText(line)
	consumed := 0
	for byteAt, character := range lineText {
		if consumed >= utf16Column {
			return index.starts[line] + byteAt
		}
		consumed += utf16RuneLen(character)
	}
	return index.starts[line] + len(lineText)
}

// utf16Offset converts one absolute UTF-8 byte offset into the absolute
// UTF-16 code-unit offset required by the compiler transport. It deliberately
// counts code points rather than grapheme clusters: a combining sequence has
// one unit for the base and one for its combining mark, matching TypeScript.
func (index *lineIndex) utf16Offset(byteOffset int) int {
	if byteOffset < 0 {
		byteOffset = 0
	}
	if byteOffset > len(index.text) {
		byteOffset = len(index.text)
	}
	if index.ascii {
		return byteOffset
	}
	checkpoint := index.utf16Checkpoints[sort.Search(len(index.utf16Checkpoints), func(i int) bool {
		return index.utf16Checkpoints[i].byteOffset > byteOffset
	})-1]
	return checkpoint.codeUnits + utf16Extent(index.text[checkpoint.byteOffset:byteOffset])
}

func utf16Extent(text string) int {
	length := 0
	for _, character := range text {
		length += utf16RuneLen(character)
	}
	return length
}

func utf16RuneLen(character rune) int {
	if character > 0xFFFF {
		return 2
	}
	return 1
}
